rules: Every gate is a separate, explicit owner decision. A GO on one gate never implies another.
Every consent phrase authorizes exactly one scope and ends with the sentence 'This does not authorize any other gate.' (the Japanese phrase ends with the matching sentence).
No gate is open today. Writing a phrase in this file is not giving it.
No secret, key, token or project ref is ever written into git, chat or a Report: a phrase names a project only by the first 12 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its ref.
A secret the executor needs is set in the executor's own environment by the owner, out of band. An AI agent never receives, types or stores one.
A harness PASS is a PASS of our orchestration on a stand-in or a model. It is never a PASS of a real remote revoke, the Vault, a managed OAuth flow or production.

decisions.question: Which login runs the pinned production inventory query?
options: a dedicated CONNECT-only login (creating it is a production write that needs consent PG2A-LOGIN)
an existing owner login in a READ ONLY session (no production write; the credential is broader than the query needs)
decisions.why: the query is pinned by SHA-256 and runs in one READ ONLY transaction either way; the dedicated login limits what a mistake could do, at the price of one production write the owner must consent to

decisions.question: How is the baseline DDL exported (PG2b)?
options: pg_dump --schema-only restricted to the listed relations by a login that holds SELECT on them (available today; reads no row, but needs a data-capable credential)
a catalog-only generator run by the CONNECT-only login (does not exist; needs a separate TASK and review)
decisions.recommended: pg_dump by the owner's own login if G4 wants to proceed now; the generator if G4 wants least privilege and accepts one more TASK
decisions.why: local evidence (section 4): a CONNECT-only login cannot run pg_dump even with --schema-only, because pg_dump takes ACCESS SHARE locks that need SELECT

decisions.question: In which organization does the disposable project live?
options: a new organization of its own (only the owner is a member)
decisions.recommended: a new organization of its own
decisions.why: membership of an organization gives access to every project in it; a separate organization makes a mix-up between the disposable and production a different login context

decisions.question: Which cost envelope does the owner accept?
options: E0: Free plan, ceiling USD 0, only if a free project slot is available
E1: a new Pro organization, ceiling USD 25, project deleted the same day
decisions.recommended: E0 if the owner's free slot is available, otherwise E1
decisions.why: the pages state two free projects across every organization the owner administers; whether a slot is free cannot be read without signing in, so it is NOT_VERIFIED here

decisions.question: Which redirect URLs does the project's Auth list hold?
options: kabumori-social://auth-callback and kabumori-social://oauth-callback, both exact, no wildcard (what F4's preflight requires)
kabumori-social://auth-callback only (what the app passes to Auth)
decisions.recommended: both exact, because F4's preflight REFUSES an auth-callback-only list and changing F4's contract is a different TASK; if the provider does not match an exact entry once a flow id is appended (Q-1), stop and go back to F4
decisions.why: offline test of the pinned F4 preflight: an auth-callback-only list fails REDIRECTS_DECLARED

decisions.question: What happens to M12 (ending POSTONA alone) on the hosted project?
options: excluded from the first managed pass and listed as BLOCKED
a deployed inert stand-in, which needs an F3 / G3 contract, a digest pin and a separate approval
F3's real saga, which holds the X revoke call and the login-deleting scope
decisions.recommended: excluded from the first managed pass; the validation of the orchestration stays on the local harness (D-2)
decisions.why: D-2's stand-in is injected at the harness boundary, not a function the project can reach; the legacy function is not deployed on the project

decisions.question: How is the project's configuration accepted?
options: the owner fills the readback sheet from the dashboard and d3_readback.ts decides
no sheet (not recommended: the repository has no config.toml)
decisions.why: Auth providers, redirects, JWT expiry, exposed schemas, function list and secret names live in the project, not in git
